text:
“We are 92 % complete.”

I have heard that sentence in progress meetings for 18 years. It has rarely told me when we would finish.

Percent complete is earned against budget hours. It tells you how much of the plan has been earned. It does not tell you how much work is left in the field, or how hard that work is.

And the last 8 % is the hardest work on the project:
• punch items spread over the whole plant
• small bore, tie-ins and supports nobody planned in detail
• test packs waiting on one missing spool
• insulation and painting held for lines that are not yet tested
• all of it at height, under permit, after the big crews have left

So 92 % can mean six weeks. It can also mean six months.

When I hear a high percentage now, I ask for three other numbers:
1. Remaining work in hours, by system, against the crews actually on site
2. The ten items that gate mechanical completion, by name and owner
3. The rate we need against the rate we achieved in the last four weeks

If those three agree with the percentage, good. If they don't, the percentage is decoration.

What is the highest “% complete” you have seen on a project that still finished more than three months late?
